target_customer: Mental health institutions and therapists in the Netherlands and Europe that license VR software and lease headsets
problem: Therapist time is scarce and some treatments such as EMDR are hard to scale. Psylaris lets clients do guided VR sessions autonomously while therapists focus on other care.
business_model: B2B software license and headset leasing to therapists and clinics, mainly subscription

founders.name: Christoph Lynen
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CTO. A Dutch profile says he founded the company in September 2017 with two fellow students and that the VR idea came from him.

founders.name: Mike Verhiel
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in a 2019 Silicon Canals interview. No source opened calls him a co-founder, so he is listed as CEO only.

competitors.name: Psious
competitors.what: Barcelona VR platform for psychologists treating phobias and anxiety
competitors.traction_then: Used by private psychologists in several countries and at Stanford and Hospital del Mar per 2016 coverage
competitors.funding_then: 1 million euro round in 2016 led by Rothenberg Ventures

technical_complexity.rationale: VR therapy software on Oculus Go with an EMDR module and a therapist dashboard, plus later CE certification as medical software. Moderate engineering with regulatory work.

defensibility.rationale: CE certification and integration into institutional workflows are hard to copy quickly, but the content can be replicated by other VR therapy vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The 2019 interview says no other company was building EMDR solutions in the Netherlands; Psious later became Amelia Virtual Care and merged into XRHealth per secondary sources.

market_need_then: Dutch mental health care (GGZ) faced long waiting lists and scarce therapist time, and VR headsets such as Oculus Go became cheap enough for clinics in 2018.

identity.visual_style: Clinical and professional B2B site in Dutch, English and German
identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence-based, stresses it supports and does not replace therapists

branding.brand_signature: Product trademark names such as Psylaris Care, Relax and EMDR-Remote

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B clinical brand with coverage in Dutch startup press, but no evidence of wider community or brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Psylaris is a small Maastricht company that is still active. It was funded by the regional investor LIOF after YC and raised a new undisclosed round in October 2025 led by Brightlands Venture Partners to expand in Western Europe. It built a CE-certified therapist-facing product line, but amounts raised remain small and unclear, so it looks like a slow niche health tech business.
notes: CB Insights reports 500 thousand dollars raised over 3 rounds with an Oct 2025 Series A label, and another report cites about 110 thousand euro seed; both are aggregator figures, so amounts are left null. The 2019 article says no other company built EMDR solutions in the Netherlands and names Clevr and Vrendle as later exposure therapy entrants, which are not recorded as they were not founding competitors. Psious source dated 2016, before the batch. Founders' education and employers not found.
